column1: X01|Separate association from causal explanation.|LinearRegression, KFold, cross_validate, residuals and RMSE.|Reserve final rows; compare a line with a mean reference; diagnose using training predictions; finish and qualify.|The prepared 2007 population fixes the country snapshot. The line and training-mean reference share folds; OOF residuals diagnose departures before final evaluation. The fitted GDP association supports a population-specific predictive statement, not an intervention effect.

X02|A lower training error is not enough.|PolynomialFeatures, StandardScaler, Ridge, Pipeline and GridSearchCV.|Compare both candidates on the same folds before choosing and opening final evidence.|Matching folds compare the line with the complete expansion–scale–Ridge recipe. Degree selection uses training evidence, so extra flexibility must earn its place before the nominated workflow predicts final rows. Residuals and fold variation qualify a small score difference.

X03|Flexibility and explanation have different costs.|ColumnTransformer, LinearRegression, DecisionTreeRegressor and common-fold CV.|Compare both prepared candidates, tune tree depth, diagnose and nominate before final evaluation.|Numeric measurements and binary flags retain their declared meanings in both pipelines. Only the tree has a depth search here; common-fold evidence and OOF residuals support nomination before final RMSE. Coefficients and tree importance have different interpretations and neither establishes causality.

X04|Future observations must not teach the past.|Chronological slicing, TimeSeriesSplit, mixed preparation and last-block diagnosis.|Sort by date/hour; reserve the final period; compare forward-validation evidence and diagnose the last training block.|The supplied file already fixes the chronological population. The final period stays later than development rows; forward folds and last-block diagnosis preserve that ordering during selection. Weather availability must still be justified for the intended prediction time.

X05|Strong scores can depend on a shortcut.|OHE, StandardScaler, LogisticRegression, macro F1 and stratified CV.|Compare C within the pipeline and inspect the context ablation using the same training folds.|Scaling and encoding are fitted inside stratified folds. The measurements-only ablation uses those same folds, exposing dependence on context without consulting final species labels. OOF confusion and macro F1 qualify a potentially strong aggregate result.

X06|Inspect validation error as complexity changes.|DecisionTreeClassifier, OneHotEncoder, GridSearchCV and confusion_matrix.|Evaluate depth choices within training folds before selecting a final tree.|Encoding preserves the Car category schema while training-fold depth comparison controls tree complexity. OOF confusion reveals class errors before final evaluation. Importance describes this fitted tree’s split reductions and must not be presented as a causal ranking.

X07|Distance reflects measurement units.|StandardScaler, KNeighborsClassifier and a pipeline neighbour grid.|Fit scaling inside folds, compare k, diagnose class errors and finish.|The scaler is inside the KNN pipeline, so each validation row is excluded from both scale estimation and the neighbour table used to predict it. Matching stratified folds compare k values, and OOF class errors qualify the selected neighbourhood before final reporting.

X08|Margin scores are not probabilities.|SVC, StandardScaler, decision_function and macro F1.|Compare C using training evidence, inspect errors and report final metrics without inventing probabilities.|The RBF pipeline learns its scale within each training fit and compares C on matching stratified folds. Class predictions support macro F1 and confusion evidence. This SVC configuration returns margin scores rather than calibrated class probabilities.

X09|One feature must carry the entire rule.|OneRPreprocessor, OneRClassifier, stratified CV and macro F1.|Evaluate the learned rule against the reference, inspect its failures and finish without a numeric-bin search.|The categorical One-R path learns a single-feature rule with the production unknown-category fallback. It is compared with the majority reference on training folds without an irrelevant numeric-bin search. Error analysis qualifies how much such a simple rule can express.

X10|Bin boundaries are learned information.|OneRPreprocessor numeric/discrete metadata and the bins grid.|Compare bin counts inside training folds, preserve binary types and explain the selected rule.|The prepared popular target is explicit, but its source winpercent is deliberately excluded from X as a leakage test. The preprocessor preserves numeric versus binary meanings, and bin boundaries are learned inside each training fit before class diagnostics and final evaluation.

X11|Match feature evidence to measurement type.|GaussianNB, var_smoothing, predict_proba and macro F1.|Compare smoothing within training folds, inspect probability/class alignment and finish.|The five continuous measurements match Gaussian likelihoods. Training-fold smoothing comparison precedes OOF diagnosis and final probability reporting, whose columns follow fitted class order. Correlated measurements limit the conditional-independence approximation and confidence interpretation.

X12|Zeros carry evidence too.|BernoulliNB, alpha, stratified CV and macro F1.|Compare smoothing using binary inputs and training evidence, then inspect errors and finish.|The input contains only the nine binary flags and the declared popular target. Bernoulli evidence includes absence as well as presence; alpha is compared on stratified training folds. Macro F1 and class diagnostics expose behaviour that overall accuracy can hide.

X13|Represent categories with indicators.|OneHotEncoder, BernoulliNB and a pipeline alpha grid.|Learn encoding inside each fit, compare smoothing, diagnose and finish.|One-hot encoding is learned within each fit and reused for validation or prediction. The production Bernoulli path models the resulting indicators, with alpha selected from training evidence. This is the supported categorical recipe, not an invented mixed-likelihood Naive Bayes model.

X14|Flexible covariance requires within-class support.|LinearDiscriminantAnalysis, QuadraticDiscriminantAnalysis, shrinkage and reg_param.|Compare both assumptions and validation evidence on the same population, then nominate before final testing.|LDA and QDA share population, features, stratified folds and scoring. Their separate shrinkage/regularisation choices are evaluated before nomination; warnings and class support qualify the more flexible covariance model. The final test evaluates the already chosen workflow.

X15|Scaled optimisation must return meaningful output units.|MLPRegressor, TransformedTargetRegressor and nested width parameters.|Keep target transformation inside fitting, compare widths and report inverse-transformed predictions.|The input is the exact fixed deduplicated 600-row sample. Feature scaling and target transformation are fitted within each neural training fit; width comparison and loss/residual evidence precede final evaluation. Predicting through the wrapper restores quality-score units for RMSE.

X16|Complexity needs evidence.|MLPClassifier, LogisticRegression and matching stratified folds.|Compare both searches and training diagnostics before choosing; either model may be defensible.|Both neural and logistic candidates use the same five measurements and stratified folds. Candidate searches, OOF class errors and neural loss histories support a nomination that can consider runtime and stability. Final evidence evaluates that decision without reopening it.

X17|No score proves natural classes.|StandardScaler, KMeans, silhouette_score and group profiles.|Combine geometry and scores with useful descriptions; state the chosen population and limitations.|The primary file contains only the four measurements, so species cannot influence fitting or k selection. Standardised geometry supports the k comparison, while aligned original-unit profiles and sizes support interpretation. A defensible grouping need not maximise one score or represent natural classes.

X18|Sample labels belong to sampled rows.|linkage, dendrogram, cut_tree and index-aligned profiles.|Scale the population, preserve sample identity through the hierarchy, compare cuts and qualify the scope.|The measurement-only population is scaled before the declared reproducible sample is selected. Original row identity is retained through Ward linkage, cuts and profiles. The 500-row cap bounds runtime, and conclusions describe the sampled rows rather than claiming assignments for all 569 observations.

X19|The picture and retained representation may have different dimensions.|PCA, explained_variance_ratio_, components_ and transform.|Choose retention from cumulative variance, label weights/scores and report the two-axis view separately.|The primary input excludes diagnosis and contains all 30 measurements. PCA is fitted on their standardised representation; cumulative variance determines the smallest retained prefix. Feature-labelled weights and row-aligned scores support interpretation, while the separate two-axis view does not claim to show the full retained information.
